inline.s: [Essential Explanation] The first section — the universal exhortation — is here concluded.
[Note] Section B1: the opening universal exhortation concludes here.
[Note] In Master Xuanzang’s translation, the Sutra of Praise for the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception, there is here still a very important passage of scripture:

Moreover, Shariputra! In this defiled, patient-enduring world, in this evil time of the five corruptions, should there be good men or good women of pure faith who, hearing this Dharma that is so hard to believe throughout all worlds, are able to give rise to faith and understanding, receive and hold it, proclaim it, and practice in accord with the teaching, you should know that such a person is extremely rare, having planted good roots in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas. At the end of life such a person will certainly be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, and enjoy the bliss of the Great Vehicle in that pure Buddha-land adorned with manifold merits and virtues. Day and night, in all six periods, he draws near to and makes offerings to the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, travels through the ten directions to make offerings to all Buddhas, and in the presence of those Buddhas hears the Dharma and receives the prophecy [of future Buddhahood]. The provisions of merit and wisdom are swiftly fulfilled, and he soon realizes unexcelled, right, and universal enlightenment.”

Please note the words “able to give rise to faith and understanding, receive and hold, proclaim, and practice in accord with the teaching, … such a person at the end of life will certainly be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.”
Section B2: Concluding Exhortation

When the Buddha had spoken this scripture, Shariputra and the assembled bhikshus, together with all the gods, humans, and asuras of the worlds, having heard what the Buddha said, joyfully believed and accepted it, and, paying homage, departed.

[Essential Explanation] This Dharma-gate is inconceivable, hard to believe and hard to understand, and there was no one able to put forth a question. The Buddha’s wisdom discerned the capacities [of beings], and knowing that their conditions for attaining Buddhahood were ripe, spoke without being asked, causing them to gain the four benefits, like the timely rain that transforms [the plants]. Hence they joyfully believed and accepted. Body and mind being at ease and joyful is called ‘joy’; being utterly free of doubt is called ‘faith’; receiving and holding so as never to forget is called ‘acceptance’; feeling the great kindness [of the Buddha] and casting oneself down in devotion is called ‘paying homage’; practicing in accord with the teaching and going forward without ever turning back is called ‘departing.’

[Note] [Causing them to gain the four benefits, like the timely rain that transforms — causing beings to gain the benefit of the four methods of exposition (catvari siddhanta); those who receive its transformation are like a sweet rain after a great drought, coming at the right time and suiting the occasion.] [Acceptance: to take in and not forget, and to practice in accord with the teaching, is called ‘acceptance.’]

The scripture says: “In the Dharma-ending age, though millions upon millions cultivate, rarely does one attain the Way; only by relying on Buddha-recitation does one gain deliverance.” Alas! Now is precisely that time. If we abandon this inconceivable Dharma-gate, how can we ever be made good
([shu] means good)
When Xu first left home, proud of the Chan lineage and disdaining the scriptural teaching, I wrongly held that name-recitation was but a method twisted toward the lower and middle capacities
(I wrongly held that the gate of Buddha-recitation was practiced by those of lower and middle faculties)
. Later, because of a grave illness I turned my resolve toward the West. Upon studying again the Miao Zong
(The Contemplation Sutra’s Essential Teaching, Miao Zong Chao)
and the Yuan Zhong
(The Amitabha Sutra’s Essential Teaching, Yuan Zhong Chao)
these two commentaries, together with Yunqi’s
(Master Lianchi)
Shu Chao
(the Amitabha Sutra Shu Chao)

and other works, only then did I know that the samadhi of Buddha-recitation is truly the supreme precious king, and only then was I willing to hold the name fast with a fixed mind, which ten thousand oxen could not drag away.
My friend Qubing
(Qubing is the pen-name of my friend)
, who had long devoted himself to the pure karma, wished to make the main purport of this sutra clear, in words not elaborate yet brilliantly lucid
([bing zhu] means conspicuous)

, and asked me to set forth an essential explanation. Desiring to be reborn together with all beings of the Dharma-realm, I could not in reason decline. I took up the brush on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month in the ding-hai year

, and finished the draft on the fifth day of the tenth month, a work of nine days in all. My wish is that a single sentence and a single character all become provisions for the path; that the one who sees and the one who hears equally ascend to the stage of no-retrogression; that the believing and the doubting alike plant the seed of the Way, and the praising and the slandering equally return to liberation. I look up only to the Buddhas and bodhisattvas to receive and certify this, and to fellow practitioners and friends to rejoice and add their blessings.
The Way-Master of the West, Xiyou
(a byname of Master Ouyi)
Ouyi Zhixu lays down the brush
(setting down the pen, meaning that the writing is finished)
and so writes this postscript, then aged forty-nine.
